title: Load a CNC tool magazine: the face mill gets empty pockets on both sides
instruction: Load the three new tools from the trays into empty pockets of the tool magazine. The face mill is a large tool: both pockets next to it must stay empty, or it will hit its neighbours at the next tool change. Leave the tools already in the magazine where they are, and let go of the tools.
context: CNC machine operators and tool setters load tools into the machine's tool magazine before a job. Tool-changer manuals define large (oversize) tools, typically face mills wider than the pocket spacing, which need the pockets on both sides left empty: otherwise the large tool strikes its neighbours when the magazine indexes or the changer arm swings. So the setter picks a pocket whose two neighbours are free and keeps them free while loading the rest. The tools already loaded stay put: in a fixed-pocket magazine the machine's tool table records which pocket holds which tool, and a tool moved to another pocket is called up as the wrong tool.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Seven kinds of thing are on the table. (1) Magazine plate: a round grey steel plate, 270 mm across and 10 mm thick, fixed to the table, centred at x 30.0 cm, y 0. (2) Eight pockets: square sockets on the plate, each made of four dark steel walls 4 mm thick and 25 mm tall around a 52 x 52 mm opening (60 mm outside), sides parallel to x and y, the plate's top as the floor, fixed. Their centres lie on a circle of radius 90 mm around the plate's centre, 45 degrees apart (68.9 mm centre to centre), numbered P1 to P8 counter-clockwise seen from above, starting straight ahead: P1 x 39.0, y 0; P2 x 36.4, y +6.4; P3 x 30.0, y +9.0; P4 x 23.6, y +6.4; P5 x 21.0, y 0; P6 x 23.6, y -6.4; P7 x 30.0, y -9.0; P8 x 36.4, y -6.4 (cm). Pockets next to each other around the ring are neighbours; P8 and P1 are neighbours. (3) A red plastic tab, 8 x 20 x 3 mm, fixed on the plate just beyond P1's far wall (centre x 42.6, y 0), marks P1. (4) Three loaded tools, all alike: steel-grey aluminium cylinders standing in for tool holders with drills and end mills, 40 mm across and 70 mm tall, 150 g each (hollow: a solid one would weigh 240 g), standing upright, centred in P1, P2 and P5. (5) Two new small tools: the same cylinders in blue, 150 g each, standing upright on the left tray at x 26.0, y +23.0 and x 16.0, y +23.0. (6) Face mill: one rigid part, a blue cylinder 40 mm across and 40 mm tall (the holder's shank) with a smooth black cylinder 76 mm across and 30 mm tall (the cutter body; no inserts or cutting edges) fixed on top on the same axis, 70 mm tall in all, 280 g (hollow aluminium; solid it would weigh 500 g), standing shank down on the right tray centred at x 20.0, y -22.0. Seated in a pocket, its cutter body's underside is 15 mm above the pocket walls. (7) Two trays: light grey plastic sheets 3 mm thick, fixed: the left one 200 x 90 mm (200 mm along x) centred at x 21.0, y +23.0; the right one 110 x 110 mm centred at x 20.0, y -22.0. Nothing else is on the table. With P1, P2 and P5 loaded, P7 is the only pocket whose two neighbours are empty (P3 is next to P2, P4 and P6 to P5, P8 to P1).
scoring: End state, read at the last step from the tools' poses (in a real trial: a photo from above with the grippers open, and a ruler). A tool is seated in a pocket when it stands upright (its axis within 5 degrees of vertical; a small tool either end down, the face mill shank down), the centre of its bottom face is inside that pocket's 52 x 52 mm opening seen from above and within 3 mm of the plate's top, and it is at rest (neither end of its axis moved more than 2 mm in the last 0.5 s). A tool is loose on the magazine when some part of it is over the plate seen from above, its lowest point is less than 75 mm above the plate's top or below it (a seated tool's top is 70 mm up), and it is not seated: lying on the plate or the walls, leaning on the plate from the table, standing on the plate outside a pocket, leaning in a pocket, upside down, standing on another tool, across two pockets, held low over it, or still moving. Score 0 if any of: (a) P1, P2 or P5 does not hold one of the three steel-grey tools loaded there, seated (they look alike, so a swap among those three pockets cannot be seen and is not scored); (b) any tool is loose on the magazine; (c) the face mill is seated in a pocket next to a pocket that holds a seated tool. Otherwise the score is the sum of: 0.5 if the face mill is seated with both neighbouring pockets empty (with P1, P2 and P5 loaded this can only be P7); 0.25 for each new small tool seated in P3 or P4, the empty pockets that leave P7 and its neighbours P6 and P8 free. A small tool seated in P6, P7 or P8 earns nothing, because it takes the face mill's only pocket or one of its neighbours (with the face mill in P7, a tool in P6 or P8 is condition (c)). A tool neither seated nor loose on the magazine (on its tray, on the table with no part over the plate, on the floor, or with its lowest point 75 mm or more above the plate) earns nothing and does not by itself make the score 0. Possible scores: 0, 0.25 (one small tool in P3 or P4), 0.5 (both small tools, or the face mill alone), 0.75 (the face mill and one small tool), 1.0 (all three). Success: 1.0 held for 2.5 s. The scorer reads only the tools, not the grippers, so a tool still held but seated and at rest counts as seated.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, default friction. The magazine is a fixed bench-scale ring: nothing indexes, swings or clamps, and the large-tool rule is scored from which pockets hold tools, as a setter checks it, not from a simulated crash. Real carousel magazines hold tools taper-up in spring forks; here they stand shank down in sockets. Masses are cut to the sim's 0.3 kg limit (real holders weigh 1-3 kg). The face mill is one rigid body of two cylinders, mass spread evenly by volume.
reset_notes: Put the three steel tools back upright in P1, P2 and P5, the two blue small tools upright on the left tray at x 26.0, y +23.0 and x 16.0, y +23.0, and the face mill shank down on the right tray at x 20.0, y -22.0; P3, P4, P6, P7 and P8 empty. Nothing is consumed.
